refusals.reason: volumes.pgdata: renamed to sf-learn_pgdata so concurrent stacks don't collide
networks.default: renamed to sf-learn_default so concurrent stacks don't collide
services.app: image renamed to sf-learn-app:dev for the isolated build
services.app: published port stripped so Docker assigns a random host port
services.db: published port stripped so Docker assigns a random host port

recipe.prepare: stackfork prepare -f examples/node-postgres/docker-compose.yml (from the stackfork repo root, --hostname optional)
login: no login; GET / returns {"visits": N}, climbing on every request

answers.question: the app service has no Docker healthcheck - should one be added, or is polling curl from the caller enough?
answers.answer: polling is enough for this example: the app already retries its own migration on startup, and ci-check.sh already polls with curl before asserting anything, so a Docker-level healthcheck would just duplicate that without adding real value here

checks: database identity (fresh Postgres volume per instance, verified via clone-db test)
app readiness (GET / returns real, incrementing Postgres-backed visit count)
two instances run side by side with independent data (ci-check.sh, real Docker)
verification.confirmation: verified via examples/node-postgres/ci-check.sh, which passed against real Docker: two worktrees ran side by side, ports and Postgres data stayed independent, and the visits counter reflected real inserted rows
